chunks: From him, from Faḍālah, from al-Sakūnī, from Abī ʿAbdillāh عليه السلام, who said:
“Indeed, the Messenger of Allah صلى الله عليه وآله kissed ʿUthmān ibn Maẓʿūn after his death.”

So the proper way regarding these two reports is that we interpret them to mean that kissing, when it is after death, is permissible before the body becomes cold or after the ghusl, because there is no harm in that according to what we have explained in the earlier reports. Those are detailed, while these are general, and the general should be carried upon the detailed; and that makes the matter even clearer.

key_terms.الْغُسْلِ: the ritual washing of the deceased
key_terms.رَسُولَ اللَّهِ: the Messenger of Allah صلى الله عليه وآله

ai.seo_question: Is it permissible to kiss a deceased person in Shia hadith?
ai.summary: This report states that the Messenger of Allah صلى الله عليه وآله kissed ʿUthmān ibn Maẓʿūn after his death. The accompanying legal explanation reconciles the narrations by understanding such kissing as permissible before the body grows cold or after the ghusl, applying detailed reports to explain general ones.
